title: Unified Inference: Product PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes (v5)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
========

This document consolidates the product requirements (PRD), high-level design, roadmap, pricing/packaging guidance, and release notes for Unified Inference v5 - the next major evolution of Redwood's unified inference product line that unifies Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments under a consistent developer and operational experience. This deliverable is intended for product, engineering, go-to-market, and customer-facing teams.

Short intro
- Objective: deliver a single, versioned API and control plane with explicit cost/latency controls, improved model routing, and an opinionated defaults surface for enterprises migrating from bespoke on-prem inference.
- Target customers: platform teams, AI-native product teams, and enterprise customers with predictable SLAs.
- Release window: phased Q2-Q4 2026 (see Roadmap).

Goals and success metrics
-------------------------
Primary goals:
1) Consistent developer experience: single API surface and SDK parity across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
2) Predictable economics: pricing tiers + autoscaling primitives that reduce 95th-percentile token cost by 15% for typical workloads.
3) Operational maturity: SLO attainment (99.9% P99 latency SLO for 3 largest enterprise customers on Dedicated) and robust rollout controls (canaries, automated fallbacks).

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Developer adoption: 30% of new sign-ups use unified API within 90 days.
- Cost improvement: mean per-token cost reduced 12-18% on benchmark workloads.
- Reliability: P99 inference latency for standard 2k sequence < 450ms for Dedicated in-region; overall platform availability >= 99.95%.
- Enterprise readiness: 3 GA Private customers onboarded with required compliance checklists.

Use cases and personas
----------------------
Primary personas:
- ML Platform Engineer: needs predictable SLAs, version pinning, and rollout controls.
- Product Engineer: wants simple SDKs and low-latency predictions for user-facing features.
- Security/Compliance Officer: requires private deployments, audit logging, and KMS integration.

Representative use cases:
- Real-time chat with streaming responses and function/tool calling.
- Embeddings at scale for search/retrieval pipelines.
- Batch reranking and summarization with configurable throughput/latency tradeoffs.

Requirements
------------
Functional requirements (MUST):
- FR-101: Single public REST/SDK API that routes to appropriate deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private) based on customer config.
- FR-102: Model catalog with model variants and quantization profiles; allow pinning by version and variant.
- FR-103: Per-route controls for batching, caching, and KV-cache TTL.
- FR-104: Canary/A-B rollout primitives with automatic rollback on quality/perf regressions.
- FR-105: Streaming and function calling support identical in all modes.

Non-functional requirements (MUST/SHOULD):
- NFR-201 (MUST): P99 inference latency targets (see SLOs) and telemetry for token-level cost/latency.
- NFR-202 (MUST): End-to-end audit logging for Private deployments integrated with customer KMS.
- NFR-203 (SHOULD): Autoscaling to handle burst traffic with <60s scale-up for Dedicated pools.
- NFR-204 (SHOULD): Quantization profiles and kernel selection to target cost/perf tradeoffs.
- NFR-205 (MUST): Backward compatibility guarantee for major surface API for 12 months post-release.

Constraints and out-of-scope
- Real-time streaming for >8k token responses is considered advanced and may be addressed in a later iteration.
- Deep model editing tooling (fine-tuning UI) is out of scope for v5.

Design specification (high-level)
--------------------------------
Architecture overview:
- Control plane: single service that manages model catalog, customer configuration, routing policies, and rollout state.
- Data plane: pluggable runtime adapters (hosted runtime, dedicated runtime, private agent) that implement a standardized gRPC transport and token accounting.
- Smart routing/fallbacks: policy engine evaluates latency, cost, region, and model compatibility; fallback hierarchy: pinned variant -> compatible variant -> cross-region fallback -> queued degrade.

Key components and interfaces:
- API gateway: exposes REST + streaming endpoints; enforces quotas and rate limits.
- Model catalog service: metadata (model id, variant, quantization profile, compatible runtimes).
- Routing policy engine: declarative policies per customer/route.
- Telemetry pipeline: token-level traces, latency histograms, and per-route cost reports.

APIs and schema examples (excerpt)
- Create route (POST /v1/routes):
  {
    "route_id": "support-chat-v1",
    "model": "redwood-unified-1",
    "deployment_mode": "dedicated",
    "batching": {"max_tokens": 4096, "latency_budget_ms": 200},
    "autoscale_policy": "replica_based"
  }

- Rollout policy example:
  - canary_percent: 10
  - metric: p99_latency_ms
  - rollback_threshold: +25% vs baseline

Performance targets and SLOs
---------------------------
- SLO-1 (Hosted API): 99.9% of requests under p95 latency 200ms for short (<=256 token) responses.
- SLO-2 (Dedicated enterprise): 99.9% availability and P99 latency < 450ms for standard 2k sequences in-region.
- SLO-3 (Private): 99.5% uptime for control plane connectivity; customer-managed infra excluded.
- Observability: Token-level cost traces, per-route error budgets, and regression detection alerts.

Roadmap and themes (Q2-Q4 2026)
--------------------------------
Q2 2026: GA readiness and core integrations
- Stabilize unified API and runtime parity across modes.
- Complete Private agent packaging and KMS integrations.
- Pricing model v1 public docs and partner enablement.

Q3 2026: Cost/performance optimizations
- Intelligent batching suggestions and automated quantization recommendations.
- Model routing heuristics for cost-aware fallbacks.
- Release SDK improvements (Python, TS) and add more sample apps.

Q4 2026: Enterprise scale and extended features
- Multi-tenant Dedicated improvements and improved autoscaling.
- Advanced canary analyses (quality score regression + A/B experiment support).
- Expanded region support and marketplace listings.

Roadmap milestones and owners
- M1 (2026-05-15): v5 internal feature complete (API parity) - Owner: Product Engineering (Elena Park).
- M2 (2026-06-30): Private GA beta with 2 reference customers - Owner: Private Deployments (Ravi Singh).
- M3 (2026-08-15): Pricing v1 public launch and docs - Owner: GTM (Maya Thompson).
- M4 (2026-10-01): Autoscaling and intelligent batching stable - Owner: Serving Runtime (Marco Alvarez).

Pricing and packaging notes
--------------------------
Pricing objectives:
- Simple to adopt for PLG users with transparent per-token pricing for Hosted.
- Predictable economics for Dedicated via committed capacity + burst pricing.
- Enterprise packaging for Private: platform license + support tier + optional observability add-on.

Proposed pricing tiers (high-level):
- Hosted (Pay-as-you-go): base per-token generation + per-embedding unit. Volume discounts at 10M/100M tokens.
- Dedicated (Committed): monthly commitment for GPU pool with committed throughput; burst pricing at 1.5x base rate.
- Private (Enterprise): annual license (fixed) + per-instance support; custom pricing for air-gapped on-prem customers.

Discounting and incentives:
- Commitment discounts for Dedicated (10-25% depending on 6/12/24 month terms).
- Migration credits for first 90 days for newly onboarded Dedicated customers.

Packaging guidance for sales
- Standard packaged SKU: Unified Inference Dedicated Starter (4 A100 equiv) + 3 months support.
- Enterprise bundle: Private license + 24/7 SLA + observability add-on + onboarding services.

Release notes (v5.0.0) - 2026-05-12
--------------------------------
Summary:
- v5 consolidates previously separate runtime APIs into the Unified Inference surface. The release focuses on API parity, model cataloging, rollout primitives, and pricing/packaging readiness.

Notable features:
- Single REST/SDK surface that transparently routes to Hosted, Dedicated, or Private.
- Model catalog with explicit quantization profiles and variant metadata.
- Canary/A-B rollout controls with metric-driven rollback.
- Token-level telemetry and per-route cost breakdowns in Console (beta).

Bug fixes and improvements:
- Fixed rare KV cache invalidation issue causing degraded latencies on long-lived sessions.
- Reduced median cold-start by 18% for dedicated pools via optimized warmup kernels.

Known issues and workarounds:
- Large cross-region fallbacks may observe transient error spikes; recommended to set fallback window to 3s for high-sensitivity routes.
- Private agent on certain legacy OS requires an additional libc patch (see onprem-packaging/runbook-2026-04-01).

Rollout and launch plan
----------------------
1) Internal canary (2026-05-12 to 2026-05-22): roll out to infra and product teams; monitor token-level telemetry and SLOs.
2) Beta customers (2026-05-25 to 2026-06-30): invite 10 targeted customers for Dedicated and 2 Private early adopters.
3) Public launch (pricing docs live) (2026-07-15): open Hosted adoption and self-serve sign-up updates.
4) Enterprise push (Q3-Q4): expand Dedicated SKUs and Professional Services engagements.

Open risks and mitigation
-------------------------
- Risk: Model parity gaps between hosted and quantized dedicated runtime may cause regressions.
  Mitigation: Maintain regression harness and mandatory model-eval gate before canary rollout.
- Risk: Customers misconfigure fallbacks and observe unexpected token costs.
  Mitigation: Provide opinionated defaults and interactive cost estimator in Console.

Appendix: sample configuration table
-----------------------------------
| Config key | Description | Default | Notes |
| route_id | Logical route name | required | Unique per customer |
| model | Model id/variant | redwood-unified-1 | Supports quantized variants |
| deployment_mode | hosted/dedicated/private | hosted | Private requires agent |
| batching.max_tokens | Max tokens per batch | 4096 | Tunable by workload |
| autoscale_policy | replica_based / latency_based | replica_based | Replica based scales by queue length |
